chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said:
I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying: When the redness disappears from this side — meaning from the direction of the east — then the sun has indeed set from the east of the earth and from its west.

key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: the redness or twilight glow visible in the sky
key_terms.غَابَتِ: disappeared or went out of sight

ai.seo_question: How is the beginning of maghrib time determined in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal sign for determining the time of maghrib. Imām Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that when the eastern redness disappears, this indicates that the sun has truly set.
